cis_text.title: Restrict Unnecessary or Unauthorized Browser and Email Client Extensions
cis_text.attribution: CIS Critical Security Controls® v8.1.2 © Center for Internet Security, Inc. Licensed under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Exact text, not changed. Use for non-commercial purposes only. Commercial use needs the prior approval of CIS. Refer to https://www.cisecurity.org/controls/ for the most up-to-date guidance. CIS does not sponsor or endorse this project.

evidence.rationale: Restricting email-client add-ins mitigates the add-in portion of this parent technique.

Disabling unauthorized Outlook add-ins prevents those add-ins from automatically loading code when the email client starts. This directly reduces persistence through email-client add-on functionality.
This technique includes browser extensions, which are directly addressed by the safeguard.

Browser extension allowlists, denylists, installation restrictions, and removal of unauthorized extensions directly prevent malicious browser extensions from establishing persistence or abusing inherited browser permissions.
Removing unnecessary or vulnerable browser plug-ins reduces components that a malicious website can enumerate and exploit during a drive-by attack.
Uninstalling unnecessary browser or email-client plug-ins removes potential client-side exploitation targets.
Malicious browser extensions may access browser cookies and session information. Restricting extensions removes one important cookie-theft path.

Malicious extensions may access credentials stored in browsers. Extension restrictions reduce that attack surface, but malware already executing with access to the browser profile may still extract stored credentials.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
'none' or 'no_row' means the mapping has no mitigating control. It does not mean that no defence exists.
Claims use ATT&CK Enterprise 16.1, the version that the source mapping uses. See later_version for changes in newer versions.
CIS claims (cis_claims and cis/safeguards) use ATT&CK Enterprise 19.1, the version that the CIS mapping uses.
